title: Empty Tomb Evidence
content: All four Gospels report that the tomb of Jesus was found empty on the third day after His crucifixion. The tomb location was known in Jerusalem, and if Jesus' body had remained there, the resurrection claim could have been easily disproven by authorities. Instead, opponents claimed that the disciples stole the body, which indirectly admits the tomb was empty. The empty tomb is one of the strongest historical evidences supporting the resurrection of Jesus.

title: Eyewitness Testimony of the Resurrection
content: The New Testament records that many people saw the risen Jesus after His resurrection. He appeared to Mary Magdalene, the disciples, and many others. The apostle Paul wrote that Jesus appeared to more than five hundred people at one time, many of whom were still alive when the letter was written. These eyewitness testimonies were circulated early in Christian history, allowing people to verify the claims. The willingness of the disciples to suffer persecution and death strengthens the credibility of their testimony.
